articles.title: Cocktail 2 Is the Most Anticipated Indian Film of the Year. The Internet Can't Pick a Side.
articles.excerpt: Shahid Kapoor, Kriti Sanon, and Rashmika Mandanna have the internet splitting into teams like it's 2012 all over again. The trailer cracked the US Top 10. June 19 cannot come fast enough.
articles.image_caption: Shahid Kapoor at a film event (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Karisma Kapoor Went to Kolkata in Peak Summer and Came Back With the Role of Her Life.
articles.excerpt: Brown is messy, divisive, and sometimes too in love with its own darkness. But Karisma as whisky-soaked detective Rita Brown is the single best performance streaming on Indian OTT right now.
articles.image_caption: Karisma Kapoor at a promotional event (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Salim Kumar Made You Laugh Until He Made You Cry. Malayalam Cinema Just Lost Its Most Versatile Soul.
articles.excerpt: The National Award-winning actor who went from Kerala's mimicry stages to the most acclaimed performance in modern Malayalam cinema died Saturday at 56. Mammootty, Prithviraj, and an entire industry are mourning a man who was never just the comic relief.
articles.image_caption: Salim Kumar, National Award-winning Malayalam actor (1969–2026)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Varun Dhawan Just Confirmed He Turned Down Andhadhun. The Original Cast Was Him and Kangana.
articles.excerpt: In a conversation with Tanmay Bhat, the actor revealed that Sriram Raghavan built one of Bollywood's greatest thrillers around him — and he walked away because his calendar was full. The internet is now imagining the film that never was.
articles.image_caption: Andhadhun (2018), directed by Sriram Raghavan, starring Ayushmann Khurrana and Tabu
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Peddi Just Crossed ₹233 Crore in Four Days. Ram Charan Doesn't Do Comebacks.
articles.excerpt: Three milestones, a $3 million North America weekend, and the definitive answer to everyone who wrote off the Mega Power Star after Game Changer.
articles.image_caption: Ram Charan in a promotional still for Peddi (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nine Films. Four Fridays. ₹1,400 Crore. June Is Bollywood's Bloodbath.
articles.excerpt: Bollywood crammed an entire year's ambition into one month. From Ram Charan's record-breaking Peddi to Shahid Kapoor's Cocktail 2 and Akshay Kumar's comeback comedy, here's your complete guide to the most competitive month Indian cinema has ever seen.
articles.image_caption: Ram Charan, whose Peddi leads June's box office charge (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: David Dhawan's Last Film Just Opened. It's Exactly the Chaos You'd Expect.
articles.excerpt: Hai Jawani Toh Ishq Hona Hai is messy, loud, and unapologetically 90s. Varun Dhawan and two leading ladies give the king of Hindi comedy the farewell he wanted — if not the numbers.
articles.image_caption: David Dhawan, the iconic Bollywood comedy director (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sonali Bendre Chose Raakh Because It Scared Her. You Should Watch It for the Same Reason.
articles.excerpt: The Paatal Lok creator's new series drops on Prime Video June 12. Ali Fazal plays a cop who can't stop thinking. Sonali Bendre plays a mother who can't stop searching.
articles.image_caption: Sonali Bendre, who returns to the screen in the investigative thriller Raakh (Wikipedia)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bhooth Bangla Just Hit Netflix. Akshay Kumar and Priyadarshan Finally Got Their Reunion Right.
articles.excerpt: The horror-comedy that earned ₹264 crore worldwide is now streaming globally. If you missed it in theatres, your excuse just expired.
articles.image_caption: Akshay Kumar, whose horror-comedy Bhooth Bangla hits Netflix on June 12 (Wikipedia)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Selena Gomez's Rare Beauty Just Landed in India. Good Luck Getting Your Hands on That Blush.
articles.excerpt: The beauty brand that conquered TikTok and redefined clean-girl makeup is now on Nykaa — online and in 30 stores. The Soft Pinch Liquid Blush alone could sell out before you finish reading this.
articles.image_caption: Selena Gomez, founder of Rare Beauty, which launched in India through Nykaa (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ragtime Won the Tony Last Night. A Musical About Immigrants and the American Dream Hit Different This Year.
articles.excerpt: Pink opened with Lady Marmalade, John Lithgow picked up his third Tony at 80, and Broadway closed its biggest season ever. The night belonged to stories about who gets to belong.
articles.image_caption: The cast of Ragtime, which won Best Revival of a Musical at the 2026 Tony Awards (Wikipedia)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Aamir Khan Personally Knocked on a Door to Steal a Title. That Film Is Now Bollywood's Biggest Independence Day Bet.
articles.excerpt: Batwara — formerly Lahore 1947 — stars Sunny Deol and his son Karan in their first-ever scene together. The teaser drops June 15. A Father's Day promo follows six days later. Here's everything we know.
articles.image_caption: Aamir Khan at a film event (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A.R. Rahman Just Performed at the India-Pakistan Border. No Artist Had Ever Done It Before.
articles.excerpt: The Oscar winner turned the Attari Beating Retreat into a concert — opening with a new melody and closing with Maa Tujhe Salaam — as thousands of BSF jawans and visitors roared along.
articles.image_caption: A.R. Rahman performing live (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Madhuri Dixit Has a Dead Body in Her Kitchen. Also, the No. 1 Spot on Netflix India.
articles.excerpt: Maa Behen is a sharp, chaotic dark comedy about a mother and two daughters covering up a crime — and Triptii Dimri steals every frame she's in.
articles.image_caption: Madhuri Dixit at a film premiere (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ranveer Singh Is Making India's First ₹300 Crore Zombie Thriller. He Dropped Don for It.
articles.excerpt: Pralay pairs him with Kalyani Priyadarshan and the son of Hansal Mehta for a post-apocalyptic survival drama that starts shooting in August.
articles.image_caption: Ranveer Singh at a promotional event (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nine Films. Four Fridays. ₹1,400 Crore on the Line. June Is Bollywood's Most Dangerous Month in Years.
articles.excerpt: After a drought that gave India five major releases in twelve weeks, Bollywood decided to dump nine in four. Trade analysts are panicking. They should be.
articles.image_caption: Shahid Kapoor — his Cocktail 2 headlines June's nine-film Bollywood battle (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Manoj Bajpayee Is Playing the Man Who Saved India From Bankruptcy. Governor Arrives June 12.
articles.excerpt: Set during the 1991 economic crisis, Governor stars Bajpayee as RBI Governor S. Venkitaramanan — the civil servant who stared down national insolvency while politicians panicked. Amit Trivedi scored it. Javed Akhtar wrote the lyrics. Your parents lived through it.
articles.image_caption: Manoj Bajpayee at a promotional event (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Main Vaapas Aaunga Arrives June 12. Imtiaz Ali Has Reunited A.R. Rahman and Irshad Kamil for a Partition Love Story. This Is Not a Drill.
articles.excerpt: Diljit Dosanjh, Naseeruddin Shah, Sharvari, and Vedang Raina star in what might be Bollywood's most emotionally loaded release of the summer — and Rahman just debuted the music at the Attari Border.
articles.image_caption: Diljit Dosanjh in Main Vaapas Aaunga (Wikipedia)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nolan's The Odyssey Opens IMAX Ticket Sales Tomorrow. India Gets First Dibs Alongside the World.
articles.excerpt: The first film ever shot entirely on IMAX cameras stars Matt Damon, Tom Holland, and Zendaya. Indian fans book tickets from June 8 — no delay, no waiting.
articles.image_caption: Christopher Nolan at a film premiere — The Odyssey is the first film shot entirely on IMAX cameras (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: David Dhawan Has Directed His Last Film. Varun Is Trying to Send Him Off With a Hit.
articles.excerpt: Hai Jawani Toh Ishq Hona Hai opened at ₹8.65 crore but flatlined on Day 2. It is a love letter from a son to his father — and a test of whether Bollywood still has room for the rom-com.
articles.image_caption: David Dhawan, Bollywood's master of comedy, on his 46th and final film (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Dhurandhar 2 Is Finally on Your TV. The Raw and Undekha Version Has 30 Minutes You Never Saw.
articles.excerpt: The ₹1,800 crore spy thriller dropped on JioHotstar this week with bonus footage, uncensored dialogue, and behind-the-scenes chaos. Netflix India follows on June 19. Your weekend just got sorted.
articles.image_caption: Ranveer Singh in Dhurandhar 2: The Revenge, now streaming on JioHotstar (Wikipedia)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bobby Deol Just Delivered the Performance of His Life. Almost Nobody Was in the Theatre to See It.
articles.excerpt: Anurag Kashyap's Bandar opened to ₹50 lakh. Then audiences started telling their friends. The TIFF-premiered prison drama is building the old-fashioned way — one stunned viewer at a time.
articles.image_caption: Bobby Deol at a film premiere (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Naseeruddin Shah Looks Exactly Like JRD Tata. Jim Sarbh Matches Him Frame for Frame. The Titan Story Is Free to Stream.

articles.image_caption: Jim Sarbh, who plays Xerxes Desai in Made In India: A Titan Story (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Parineeti Chopra Sang Chamkila. Now She's Singing Bhajans. Motherhood Changed Everything.

articles.image_caption: Parineeti Chopra at a public appearance (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Gullak Season 5 Is Here. The Mishras Have Wi-Fi Now. They're Still Fighting About Money.

articles.title: Lagaan Returns to Theatres for Three Days Only. Twenty-Five Years Later, It Still Makes You Want to Stand Up and Cheer.
articles.excerpt: The Oscar-nominated cricket epic that turned a dusty village into the most famous pitch in Indian cinema is back on the big screen — June 12 to 14. Here's why you shouldn't miss it.

articles.excerpt: Their first film together — an untitled action thriller directed by Vamshi Paidipally — moves to Mumbai for chases, combat, and crowd-heavy sequences across one of the city's most iconic neighbourhoods.

articles.title: Aamir Khan Is Getting Married Again. This Time, He Says, He Got It Right.

articles.title: Singeetham Srinivasa Rao Is 94. His New Film Has No Dialogue. Every Word Is a Song.

articles.image_caption: Legendary filmmaker Singeetham Srinivasa Rao
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Cocktail 2 Is the Most Anticipated Indian Film on IMDb. It Has Already Recovered Half Its ₹150 Crore Budget.

articles.title: Salim Kumar Is on a Ventilator. The Man Who Made Malayalam Cinema Laugh Is Fighting for His Life.
articles.excerpt: The National Award-winning actor, 56, has been rushed to a private hospital in Ernakulam. He had a liver transplant years ago and has been battling health issues since.

articles.title: House of the Dragon Returns June 21. The Targaryens Have Never Looked This Dangerous.
articles.excerpt: Season 3 of the Game of Thrones prequel premieres on HBO and JioHotstar with Hindi, Tamil, and Telugu dubs. Eight episodes. Weekly drops. The Battle of the Gullet is finally here.

articles.title: Selena Gomez's Rare Beauty Has Launched in India Through Nykaa. It Is Available in 30 Stores Today.

articles.title: A.R. Rahman Will Perform at the Attari Border Tomorrow. The Last Time He Played a Venue This Symbolic, He Won an Oscar.
articles.excerpt: The Jai Ho concert at the India-Pakistan border is a promotional event for Imtiaz Ali's partition film Main Vaapas Aaunga. It may also be the most emotionally charged performance of the year.
